_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.2 'Three tools, three jobs' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): encryption, hashing, digital signature, with the guide's pictures and RSSO examples. Computed live with Web Crypto (AES-GCM 256, SHA-256, ECDSA P-256). Every record and amount is fictional.

scenes.title: Lock: the backup is encrypted
scenes.text: A fresh 256-bit key scrambles the record. What sits on the backup drive is meaningless without the key.

scenes.title: A thief takes the drive, but not the key
scenes.text: Any other key fails. The stolen drive gives away nothing: **encryption protects Secret**.

scenes.title: The key custodian opens it
scenes.text: Ana, the named key custodian, holds the key apart from the drive. With it, the record comes back exactly.

scenes.title: Seal: a fingerprint of the payout file
scenes.text: When Director Eva approves the batch, its SHA-256 fingerprint is recorded. Any copy can be checked against it later.

scenes.title: One digit changes: 3,000 becomes 8,000
scenes.text: The fingerprint changes completely. Nobody can change the file without it showing: **hashing protects Correct**.

scenes.title: Passwords are stored as hashes
scenes.text: The portal keeps the fingerprint of each password, never the password itself. At sign-in it hashes what you type and compares.

scenes.title: Sign: the RSSO signs the payout list
scenes.text: The RSSO signs the list with its **private key**, which never leaves the office. The e-wallet provider holds the RSSO's **public key**.

scenes.title: The provider checks the signature
scenes.text: The signature matches the RSSO's public key and the file: it came from the RSSO, and nothing was changed on the way.

scenes.title: Someone swaps the wallet number on the way
scenes.text: EW-0417 becomes EW-9911. The signature no longer matches the file, so the provider rejects it.

scenes.title: An impostor sends their own list
scenes.text: It claims to come from the RSSO, but it was signed with someone else's key. Checked against the RSSO's public key, it fails: **a signature proves who sent it**.

closing: Lock, seal, sign. And **encryption without key management is false comfort**: keep keys apart from the data, with a named custodian.
